stories.title: CISA Adds Four Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
stories.abstract: CISA has added four critical vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, including flaws in Microsoft IKE, SharePoint, VMware vCenter, and Apple macOS. Additionally, GitLab released patches for multiple vulnerabilities, including one currently under active exploitation.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities are confirmed to be exploited in the wild, posing a high risk of unauthorized access or system compromise.
stories.action: Update GitLab, macOS, Microsoft, and VMware software to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: Attackers Exploit Zimbra SNMP Flaw for Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
stories.abstract: Zimbra has released security updates for its Collaboration Suite to address multiple vulnerabilities, including several now confirmed as actively exploited. CISA has added these flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, highlighting the risk of remote code execution and command injection.
stories.why: Active exploitation of these vulnerabilities allows attackers to gain full control over exposed Zimbra Collaboration Suite instances.
stories.action: Update Zimbra Collaboration Suite to version 10.1.20 or later immediately.

stories.title: Black Hat Asia 2026 | Bypassing Authentication Reflection Mitigations for SYSTEM Shells
stories.abstract: Researchers discovered that Microsoft's initial patches for CVE-2025-33073 failed to fully resolve the underlying authentication reflection flaws. The team developed a methodology to bypass these mitigations, successfully achieving SYSTEM-level execution through new NTLM and Kerberos-based privilege escalation techniques.
stories.why: Authentication reflection remains a critical vector for full system compromise, and incomplete vendor patches leave previously secured Windows environments vulnerable to exploitation.
stories.action: Ensure all Windows systems are fully updated with the latest security patches from Microsoft.

stories.title: TrueConf security advisory (AV26-835)
stories.abstract: CISA has added two vulnerabilities affecting TrueConf Server versions 5.3.x, 5.4.x, and 5.5.x to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. These flaws are currently being leveraged in active attacks, necessitating immediate attention from administrators managing these specific server deployments.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities are confirmed to be under active exploitation, posing a significant risk of compromise for organizations running affected TrueConf Server instances.
stories.action: Update TrueConf Server to version 5.3.9, 5.4.9, 5.5.5, or later immediately.

stories.title: Named Pipes Under Attack: Securing Windows Interprocess Communication
stories.abstract: Windows named pipes are increasingly targeted by attackers who exploit loose access controls to compromise privileged services. Security researchers emphasize that improper configuration allows unauthorized processes to interact with sensitive system components, necessitating stricter input validation and granular permission management.
stories.why: Misconfigured named pipes provide a common lateral movement and privilege escalation vector for attackers operating within a compromised Windows environment.

stories.title: CISA Malcolm
stories.abstract: CISA has issued an advisory for the Malcolm network traffic analysis tool, detailing multiple vulnerabilities including path traversal, arbitrary file uploads, and resource exhaustion. These flaws could permit remote attackers to execute unauthorized code or trigger denial-of-service conditions on affected systems.
stories.why: Exploitation of these vulnerabilities in network monitoring infrastructure could lead to full system compromise or significant disruption of security visibility.
stories.action: Update Malcolm to version 26.07.2 or later.

stories.title: Citrix security advisory (AV26-645) – Update 2
stories.abstract: Citrix has released security updates for NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway to address multiple critical vulnerabilities. Reports indicate that at least two of these flaws, CVE-2026-8451 and CVE-2026-8452, are currently being exploited in the wild.
stories.why: NetScaler appliances are high-value targets for initial access; active exploitation of these vulnerabilities poses a significant risk of unauthorized network entry.
stories.action: Update NetScaler ADC and Gateway to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: MLflow security advisory (AV26-832)
stories.abstract: MLflow versions prior to 3.15.0 contain a critical server-side request forgery vulnerability. Attackers can bypass webhook URL validation through malicious HTTP redirects or DNS rebinding, allowing for unauthorized read access to internal network resources.
stories.why: This flaw is actively exploited in the wild, posing a significant risk to internal infrastructure and sensitive data accessible via the MLflow server.
stories.action: Update MLflow to version 3.15.0 or later immediately.

stories.title: Microsoft Defender's Own Driver Can Be Weaponized to Delete Security Software at Boot
stories.abstract: Researchers discovered that Microsoft Defender's legitimate boot-time remediation driver, BTR.sys, can be manipulated to perform unauthorized kernel-level modifications. By leveraging this signed driver, attackers can delete security software or alter registry keys during the system startup process without needing external malicious tools.
stories.why: This technique allows attackers to disable security controls using trusted, signed Microsoft components, effectively bypassing standard endpoint protection mechanisms.

stories.title: CISA orders feds to patch actively exploited TrueConf Server flaws
stories.abstract: CISA has mandated that federal agencies address two critical vulnerabilities within the TrueConf Server platform. These flaws are currently being leveraged by malicious actors in active exploitation campaigns, necessitating immediate remediation to secure self-hosted communication infrastructure.
stories.why: Active exploitation of communication servers poses a significant risk of unauthorized access, data interception, and potential lateral movement within internal networks.
stories.action: Apply the latest security updates provided by TrueConf to patch the identified vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Hackers poison popular Rust crates to steal developers' credentials
stories.abstract: Threat actors compromised a maintainer account for the Rust crate arrayref, injecting malicious code into updates. This supply chain attack executed infostealer malware on developer machines during the standard build process, potentially harvesting sensitive credentials and environment data.
stories.why: Compromised build dependencies allow attackers to execute arbitrary code within secure development environments, bypassing perimeter defenses and compromising source code integrity.
stories.action: Audit project dependencies and review build logs for unauthorized crate versions or unexpected network activity.

stories.title: Critical macOS, SharePoint, vCenter, and Microsoft IKE Flaws Under Active Exploitation
stories.abstract: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog to include four critical security flaws currently being leveraged in real-world attacks. Among these is a severe authentication bypass vulnerability in Apple macOS, which carries a maximum CVSS score of 9.8.
stories.why: Active exploitation of critical vulnerabilities in widely used enterprise software and operating systems significantly increases the risk of unauthorized system access and compromise.
stories.action: Apply the latest security updates for macOS, SharePoint, vCenter, and Microsoft IKE immediately.

stories.title: GitLab CVE-2026-19478 Comes Under Active Exploitation Within Days of Disclosure
stories.abstract: GitLab is currently facing active exploitation of CVE-2026-19478, a critical code injection vulnerability. Unauthenticated attackers can leverage this flaw to modify or delete public project data, posing a significant risk to self-managed instances.
stories.why: This critical vulnerability allows unauthorized data manipulation, and the lack of granular detection telemetry complicates incident response for self-hosted environments.
stories.action: Apply the latest GitLab security patches immediately.

stories.title: Microsoft sounds alarm as perfect-10 Entra ID flaw comes under attack
stories.abstract: Microsoft has confirmed that a critical vulnerability in Entra ID, previously known as Azure AD, has been actively exploited in the wild. While the company has already deployed a patch to resolve the issue, they have withheld details regarding the attackers or scope.
stories.why: Identity providers are high-value targets; compromised Entra ID instances allow attackers to bypass authentication and gain persistent access to enterprise cloud environments.
stories.action: Review Entra ID sign-in logs for anomalous activity and ensure all security updates are applied.

stories.title: AI-Generated Exploit Scripts Target Siemens S7 PLCs in U.S. Critical Infrastructure
stories.abstract: U.S. authorities have issued an alert regarding threat actors utilizing AI-generated scripts to conduct reconnaissance and develop exploits against Siemens S7 programmable logic controllers. While focused on Siemens hardware, the campaign highlights a broader risk to industrial control systems exposed to the internet.
stories.why: AI-assisted exploitation lowers the barrier for adversaries to target specialized industrial hardware, increasing the risk of compromise for critical infrastructure.
stories.action: Remove Siemens S7 PLCs from internet access and apply all available security patches.

stories.title: Elementor Pro Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Upload PHP and Execute Code
stories.abstract: A critical vulnerability in the Elementor Pro WordPress plugin's Forms module allows unauthenticated attackers to upload malicious files. This flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-32475, enables remote code execution on affected servers, posing a severe risk to site integrity and control.
stories.why: Remote code execution vulnerabilities in widely used plugins provide attackers with full server access, facilitating data theft, site defacement, or malware distribution.
stories.action: Update Elementor Pro to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Microsoft Patches Severe Entra ID Flaw (CVSS 10.0) Allowing Remote Code Execution
stories.abstract: Microsoft released 22 security patches addressing various vulnerabilities across its ecosystem, including critical flaws in the Entra ID identity platform. While initial documentation suggested active exploitation, the company later clarified that these Entra ID vulnerabilities have not been leveraged in real-world attacks.
stories.why: Identity platforms are high-value targets for lateral movement and persistence; patching these flaws is essential to maintaining secure access control.
stories.action: Apply the latest Microsoft security updates to all affected systems.

stories.title: Rust Supply Chain Attack Linked to North Korean Hackers
stories.abstract: Threat actors associated with North Korea have compromised the Rust ecosystem by injecting a malicious backdoor into the arrayref package. This supply chain attack forces affected versions to retrieve and execute unauthorized payloads from an external server.
stories.why: This incident demonstrates a persistent effort to compromise software supply chains via legitimate package repositories to facilitate remote code execution.
stories.action: Audit Rust dependencies for the compromised arrayref package and update to a verified, clean version.

stories.title: Zombie Card Attack Can Revive Expired Visa Cards for Contactless Payments
stories.abstract: Researchers discovered a method to revive expired Visa contactless cards by manipulating the expiration date transmitted to point-of-sale terminals. The technique, dubbed Zombie Card, exploits NFC communication protocols to bypass validation without compromising the underlying cryptographic security of the payment card.
stories.why: This vulnerability highlights a critical flaw in how payment terminals verify card data, potentially allowing fraudulent transactions using deactivated financial credentials.

stories.title: TikTok will pay $400 million to settle Justice Department lawsuit over child privacy
stories.abstract: TikTok has agreed to a $400 million settlement with the U.S. Department of Justice to resolve allegations that the platform violated the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act by harvesting data from minors without parental consent or proper account deletion protocols.
stories.why: This settlement highlights the significant regulatory and financial risks associated with failing to implement robust age-gating and data privacy controls for minor users.

stories.title: Spring security advisory (AV26-842)
stories.abstract: The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security has issued an advisory regarding multiple vulnerabilities impacting various Spring framework components, including Spring AI, Spring Security, Spring Cloud, and Spring Data REST. Administrators should review the official Spring security portal for specific version details and remediation guidance.
stories.why: Widespread vulnerabilities in core Java frameworks pose significant risks to enterprise application integrity and data confidentiality.
stories.action: Review the official Spring security advisory and apply available patches for affected components.

stories.title: Russian network monitoring firm confirms cyberattack claimed by pro-Ukraine hackers
stories.abstract: Russian network monitoring company Microolap acknowledged a security breach following claims by the pro-Ukraine group Black Spark. The attackers reportedly maintained unauthorized access to internal systems and the EtherSensor traffic analysis platform for over a month.
stories.why: Compromised network monitoring tools can be leveraged for supply chain attacks, lateral movement, or deep reconnaissance within sensitive infrastructure.

stories.title: VMware security advisory (AV26-763) – Update 1
stories.abstract: CISA has added CVE-2026-59310 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, confirming active exploitation. The flaw impacts various VMware products, including ESXi, vCenter, Cloud Foundation, and Workstation. Administrators must prioritize patching these systems to mitigate the risk of unauthorized access or compromise.
stories.why: Active exploitation of core virtualization infrastructure poses a critical risk to enterprise environments, potentially allowing attackers to gain full control over host systems.
stories.action: Update ESXi, vCenter, and related VMware products to the versions specified in VMSA-2026-00 immediately.

stories.title: Mozilla security advisory (AV26-840)
stories.abstract: Mozilla has released security updates for Firefox, Firefox ESR, and Thunderbird to address multiple vulnerabilities. Users running older versions of these applications are exposed to potential security risks and should move to the latest patched releases immediately.
stories.why: Unpatched browser and email client vulnerabilities are primary vectors for remote code execution and system compromise.
stories.action: Update Firefox, Firefox ESR, and Thunderbird to the latest available versions.

stories.title: SilkParasite Espionage Campaign Targets Central Asian Governments with Five New RATs
stories.abstract: A Chinese-linked espionage campaign named SilkParasite is targeting Central Asian government entities. The operation utilizes seven distinct remote access trojans, five of which are newly identified, and reportedly leverages artificial intelligence to assist in the development of its malicious toolset.
stories.why: The use of AI-generated malware and a large, previously unknown arsenal of RATs indicates a sophisticated, evolving threat actor targeting regional government infrastructure.

stories.title: Isolated-vm Flaw Lets Sandboxed JavaScript Escape to Host for Potential RCE
stories.abstract: A critical type confusion vulnerability in the isolated-vm library allows attackers to bypass sandbox protections. By exploiting this flaw, unauthorized actors can achieve remote code execution on the host system through V8 sandbox escape and control-flow hijacking.
stories.why: This flaw compromises the fundamental isolation boundary between untrusted code and the host environment, posing a severe risk to applications relying on this sandbox.
stories.action: Update isolated-vm to a version beyond 7.0.0 immediately.

stories.title: Apple security advisory (AV26-839)
stories.abstract: Apple has released security updates for Safari, iOS, iPadOS, and macOS Tahoe to address newly identified vulnerabilities. Users should verify their current software versions and apply the latest patches to ensure their systems remain protected against potential exploits.
stories.why: Unpatched vulnerabilities in core operating systems and browsers are primary targets for remote code execution and privilege escalation attacks.
stories.action: Update Safari, iOS, iPadOS, and macOS Tahoe to the latest versions immediately.

stories.title: Private equity firm Apollo confirms data breach amid hacking wave targeting financial giants
stories.abstract: Private equity firm Apollo Global Management has acknowledged a data breach. This incident follows recent warnings from Google security researchers regarding a coordinated campaign by threat actors specifically targeting major financial institutions.
stories.why: Financial services remain a primary target for sophisticated threat actors, highlighting systemic risks to sensitive corporate and investor data.

stories.title: Splunk security advisory (AV26-838)
stories.abstract: Cisco and Splunk have released security updates addressing multiple vulnerabilities across their product lines, including Splunk Enterprise, Universal Forwarder, SOAR, and various Cisco networking and application platforms. Administrators should review the latest advisories to identify specific version requirements for their deployments.
stories.why: Unpatched vulnerabilities in core infrastructure and security management tools can provide attackers with unauthorized access or remote code execution capabilities.
stories.action: Review the Splunk and Cisco security advisories and update affected software to the specified versions.

stories.title: Grok exfiltrates user data when malicious instructions are encrypted
stories.abstract: Researchers have identified a technique called Cryptographic Context Injection that hides malicious prompts from AI safety filters. By encrypting instructions, attackers can bypass guardrails, as the content is only decrypted and executed once it reaches the model's trusted environment.
stories.why: This represents a significant escalation in prompt injection, rendering traditional input sanitization and safety filtering ineffective against obfuscated malicious payloads.

stories.title: U.S. Bank says breach claims related to fourth-party incident
stories.abstract: U.S. Bank confirmed that recent data breach allegations stem from a security incident at a third-party service provider. The financial institution stated that its internal networks and proprietary data systems remain secure and were not directly impacted by the event.
stories.why: Supply chain vulnerabilities remain a critical vector for data exposure, even when primary systems are not directly breached.

stories.title: Take-Two subpoenas Discord and Microsoft in hunt for GTA VI leaker
stories.abstract: Take-Two Interactive has issued subpoenas to Microsoft and Discord to identify individuals responsible for leaking proprietary Grand Theft Auto VI assets. The publisher aims to uncover the identities of those distributing unauthorized audiovisual content and creative elements ahead of the game's official launch.
stories.why: This highlights the legal mechanisms companies use to track down leakers and the potential for platform data to be compelled in copyright disputes.

stories.title: Johnson Controls Simplex Incident Manager
stories.abstract: Johnson Controls Simplex Incident Manager versions 2.01 and earlier contain a vulnerability where sensitive authentication data is stored in cleartext within system memory. Local attackers with low-level access can exploit this to harvest credentials and gain unauthorized control over the application.
stories.why: Credential exposure in critical infrastructure management software facilitates lateral movement and unauthorized access to sensitive facility control systems.
stories.action: Update Simplex Incident Manager to a version beyond 2.01.

stories.title: Canada’s Hospital for Sick Children attacked by cybercriminals again as employee data stolen
stories.abstract: Toronto's Hospital for Sick Children confirmed a data breach involving a third-party software provider. The incident resulted in the unauthorized access and theft of employee information, marking another security challenge for the institution following a major ransomware attack in 2022.
stories.why: Supply chain vulnerabilities remain a critical vector for healthcare organizations, highlighting the risks associated with third-party software dependencies.

stories.title: SickKids data breach exposes employee and job applicant info
stories.abstract: Toronto's SickKids hospital confirmed a data breach involving third-party software that exposed personal details of current staff, former employees, and job applicants. The incident did not impact patient records or clinical operations.
stories.why: Third-party software vulnerabilities remain a primary vector for unauthorized access to sensitive internal personnel data.

stories.title: Who Got Missed in the MFA Rollout? More Powershell + Graph + Entra scripting!, (Fri, Aug 21st)
stories.abstract: SANS ISC provides a practical PowerShell script leveraging the Microsoft Graph API to identify Entra ID accounts that have not yet registered for multi-factor authentication, streamlining the final stages of identity security rollouts.
stories.why: Identifying MFA gaps is critical to closing attack vectors, as unmanaged accounts are primary targets for credential stuffing and account takeover.
stories.action: Audit your Entra ID environment using the provided script to identify and remediate non-compliant user accounts.

stories.title: Android Car Malware Spreads Through Built-In Updaters for Ad Fraud, Proxy Botnet
stories.abstract: Researchers identified a malware strain targeting DoFun-developed firmware within Android-based automotive head units. The malicious code leverages legitimate system update mechanisms to install a multi-stage downloader, ultimately facilitating ad fraud and integrating the compromised vehicles into a proxy botnet infrastructure.
stories.why: Automotive firmware compromises represent a significant supply chain risk, turning vehicle infotainment systems into persistent nodes for botnet operations and unauthorized network traffic.

stories.title: Even MOAR Powershell, looking at Entra logins - the good, the bad and the password sprays, (Fri, Aug 21st)
stories.abstract: Security professionals often neglect cloud environment monitoring, specifically Entra login logs. Despite the shift to cloud infrastructure, organizations frequently fail to maintain the same level of rigorous daily log analysis that was standard practice for on-premises systems.
stories.why: Neglecting cloud authentication logs leaves organizations blind to password spraying attacks and unauthorized access attempts targeting identity providers.
stories.action: Implement automated daily monitoring and alerting for Entra sign-in logs.

stories.title: [Control Systems] Johnson Controls security advisory (AV26-837)
stories.abstract: Johnson Controls has disclosed multiple security vulnerabilities impacting several product lines, including Airwall, various versions of Metasys, and TL280 hardware. Administrators must review the manufacturer's security advisories to identify specific exposure and determine the appropriate remediation paths for their environments.
stories.why: Unpatched vulnerabilities in building automation and control systems can provide attackers with unauthorized access to critical infrastructure and facility management networks.
stories.action: Review Johnson Controls security advisories and apply available patches for Airwall, Metasys, and TL280 systems.

stories.title: Banking Trojans Manic, Grandoreiro, ToxicPanda 2.0 in the Spotlight
stories.abstract: Recent reports highlight a surge in banking trojan activity, specifically focusing on the persistent Grandoreiro campaigns across Europe and Latin America, the emergence of the spyware-capable Manic, and the updated ToxicPanda 2.0 malware targeting financial institutions.
stories.why: These evolving banking trojans demonstrate increased sophistication and geographic reach, posing significant risks to financial data integrity and user account security.

stories.title: Post-DEF CON Chaos: WiFi Pineapple Plane Panic, Mythos Commits Felonies, and Lazarus Goes Zero-Day
stories.abstract: Following DEF CON, reports emerged regarding a WiFi Pineapple incident on an airplane that gained mainstream media attention. The event highlights ongoing concerns about unauthorized wireless interception and the potential for public disruption during high-profile security conferences.
stories.why: Demonstrates the risks of portable rogue access points in confined public spaces and the increasing visibility of offensive hardware in mainstream news.
